output.summary: Approve independently reviewed G1036 revision4 under existing delegation, preserving WD1–WD8 and anonymization. Whitepaper remains practitioner-first with ratios/trends, source/trace binding and truthful observations/limitations. Base-only no-checkpoint review budget exemption and actual card-size target/exception are accurate. Design approval does not start writing: root waits for G1037 merge and report before test_design/implement. Blog is drafted only; owner publishes externally.

responses.review_design:3:1: fixed: §3 item7.6/T8/§7/W15–W16 apply G1039 exact exemption for stale base-only-input nodes with no checkpoint outputs even when they raise material findings; contrast normal charging for refused-carry checkpoint nodes and changed-subject reviews; trace evidence includes stale keys, output types and actual counters.
responses.review_design:3:2: fixed: describe4096bytes as target with known oversized-previous fixed point, cite existing test and review8537byte observation, report actual sizes/overruns, add limitation and W18 checked-build evidence requirement. output.summary: Revision4 fixes the two factual review findings without expanding scope: the sync-focused no-checkpoint review is budget-exempt when stale only on git.base-selecting inputs even if it raises material findings, while changed-subject/checkpoint cases count normally. Card4096bytes is a target with the checked build's documented oversized-previous exception; observed sizes, limitations and acceptance evidence replace the unsupported hard-bound claim. WD1–WD8 and the dogfood-merge/report writing gate remain unchanged.

findings.text: T8 says that after clean sync a 'genuinely new material finding' spends a stage-budget round, but G1039 revision 3 §3.5 explicitly exempts a node with no checkpoint outputs that started stale only on base-selecting inputs, even when it raises findings. The normal example is exactly T8's sync-focused review_impl. A checkpointing node whose carry was refused, or a review also stale on changed code, counts normally; a new finding from the exempt clean-sync review does not. Fix §3 item 7.6, T8, §7 evaluation definitions and W15/W16 to state the exemption precisely, and make the trace/check distinguish exempt base-only review findings from genuinely chargeable new material rounds rather than asserting that every new finding is charged.

The paper plan still presents 4,096 bytes as a hard card bound (§3 item 6, also 'bounded task card' in item 1), but the checked engine intentionally returns an oversized fixed point when previous cannot shrink. At read_dev de5640d, .agents/test_engine_card_budget.py::ShrinkBudgetTests::test_a_card_over_budget_because_of_previous_is_a_fixed_point passes and its fixture emits 8,537 bytes with zero remaining shrink candidates. G1039 revision 3 §3.4/§7 explicitly preserves this limitation; G1019 is open in Release 2 and is not a writing prerequisite. Fix the definition/evidence plan to describe a 4,096-byte target plus the known re-review/previous exception, cite the test and report observed overruns honestly. Add a matching limitation and acceptance check; claim a strict bound only if the final checked build actually fixes it. This needs no new engine scope or dependency.

output.summary: Approved revision 4: both prior findings are resolved. Budget wording and evidence checks now preserve G1039’s exact finding-raising clean-sync exemption; card-size claims state the target and measured oversized-previous exception. Owner choices, anonymity and the G1037 merge/report writing gate are unchanged.

spec:
Publish a long-form, linkable, print-friendly whitepaper on the repository's GitHub-hosted docs path, linked from README, that coins deterministic progressive disclosure: a pure frontier derives each agent's next action and a per-node task card disclosing only that node's prompt, selected policy instructions and inputs from Git state. Explain the mechanism as the reset built it: goal documents on per-goal branches with CAS writes, lease branches, the declarative workflow.json graph with review and human approve nodes, findings and corrections, tree/change identities and fingerprint staleness, stacked PRs with carry-forward, policy branches that pause work, and releases. Include one synthetic end-to-end trace and accessible diagrams, and state limitations candidly (advisory routing, no comprehension proof, what R1-R15 gave up). Claims bind to an explicit engine version and are checked against it. Changed from the old wording: drop heartbeats, receipts, storage locks, linear stacks and model-effort binding, and describe the Release 1 lens-based default graph.

Migrated from GitHub issue #490 after the engine reset (#740).

Order (owner, 2026-11-01): "whitepaper should be after dogfood run". Write it after G1037, from the engine as released and the private-app dogfood run notes (real goals, a real release, measured costs), and include the git-flow release branching (G1025), capabilities (G1027) and owner-question interviews (G1026).

Replaces G1002 (its branch was deleted to remove a private name, owner decision 2026-11-01).
title: Write and publish the ZzzOps whitepaper on deterministic progressive disclosure
